subject: TOURNAMENT QA-04 (CRITICAL): deliverFlag hands tournament challenge flags in PLAINTEXT to any anonymous signed-in caller - the admin console's add-box-to-tournament flow copies flag text out of flag_registry and never sets deliveryDisabled, so moving flagHash/flagSalt (task 401) does NOT close the plaintext path
description:
PROVEN by Mallory 2026-09-17, in the emulator, with production untouched. This is a SECOND route to the same secrets and it does not go through the hash at all, which is why high-entropy flags do not mitigate it.

THE PATH:
functions/index.js:672-734 deliverFlag returns a box's flag text to ANY caller with request.auth - anonymous sign-in qualifies - unless flag_registry/{boxId}.deliveryDisabled is truthy. The function's own comment documents this as deliberate for teaching labs (SPOILER-class, not forgery-class) and names the exact condition under which it collapses: 'For a RANKED competition that distinction collapses: seeing the flag IS having it, so a spoiler is a forgery.'
_app/admin/console.html:11561-11624 (add box to tournament) reads flag_registry/{boxId}.flags and copies the SAME text into the challenge doc. It never reads, checks, or sets deliveryDisabled. So the tournament-authoring workflow as built ALWAYS produces this exposure unless an admin separately remembers to lock the box afterwards, and nothing prompts or enforces it.
box_flags.json entries for both boxIds actually used by the two live tournaments (forensics-05-email, c1-data-nexus-breach) have NO deliveryDisabled key.

REPRODUCTION (emulator, second-channel verified):
Seeded flag_registry/forensics-05-email from the real box_flags.json content. Signed in anonymously via the Auth emulator (fresh uid, no prior box interaction). POST to deliverFlag with {boxId:'forensics-05-email', flagId:'user'} returned the plaintext flag; same for 'root'. Verified by an INDEPENDENT admin-SDK read that users/{anonUid}/flag_deliveries now holds forensics-05-email_user and _root with real timestamps - the disclosure actually happened rather than being a claimed response.

WHY IT MATTERS THAT THIS IS SEPARATE FROM 401: task 401 removes flagHash/flagSalt from client reach. It does nothing here. A student - or anyone with an anonymous session - can request the plaintext for a tournament's boxId directly. If 401 ships alone, October runs with the crypto fields locked down and the answers still walking out the front door.

FIX CLASS (not designed, needs the vote/operator): enforce deliveryDisabled at the point a box BECOMES a tournament challenge - in the admin console add-box flow, and/or defensively inside deliverFlag by refusing boxIds that are challenges of a lobby/active/frozen/ended tournament. Prefer the server-side check: a console-only fix is a request, not a control, and pre-existing tournaments would remain exposed.

COMPOUNDING CONTEXT: Mallory separately recovered ALL 5 live challenge flags by hashing known box_flags.json candidates against the exposed salts (task 401, Route A). The two routes confirm each other - the tournament flags ARE box flag values, so they are reachable both by offline hashing and by asking deliverFlag.
